description:
Where can we stop with the dog along this highway, in driving order: rest areas, travel stops with dog parks, hotels, campgrounds, parks and beaches, each with its mile and distance off the road?
For a drive on I-5, US-101, Highway 1, I-15, I-80 or US-50 in California, or I-15, I-80, US-50, US-95 or US-93 in Nevada (each route stops at the state line). It lists stops, not closures or chain controls.
Inputs: route (default i-5), a start as near={lat, lon} or from_mile, direction (north, south, east, west), ahead_miles or to_mile, dog_weight_lb and max_total_fee for stays. On I-5 add family=true (restrooms and a pet area stated by the source) or paired=true (an exit with places for people, plus the nearest dog-legal place).
Each stop has its mile, side, distance off the road, dog rule, source URL and verified date; stays carry the whole-stay pet fee. On I-5 a rest area Caltrans reports fully closed right now carries closed_now (Caltrans' reason and end time), is left out of the "first open stop" in the text, and stays in the list.

Examples:
  - "Driving north on I-5 from Los Angeles with a 70 lb dog, where can we stop?" -> near={lat:34.05, lon:-118.24}, direction="north", dog_weight_lb=70
  - "Pet areas on the Grapevine" -> from_mile=170, to_mile=222, kinds=["rest_area","park"]
  - "Next restroom stop for the whole family, dog included, 40 miles north of Harris Ranch" -> near={lat:36.25, lon:-120.25}, direction="north", ahead_miles=40, family=true
  - "Heading south on 101 from San Francisco, where can the dog run?" -> route="us-101", near={lat:37.77, lon:-122.42}, direction="south"
  - "Driving I-80 east from Reno with a dog" -> route="i-80-nevada", near={lat:39.53, lon:-119.81}, direction="east"

ahead_miles.description: Window in miles from the start (near or from_mile) in the direction of travel; an alternative to to_mile

direction.description: Direction of travel. Route miles increase going north, or east on I-80 and US-50; north and east both mean increasing miles

dog_friendly_only.description: Leave out stops where dogs are not allowed

family.description: Only stops whose official source states restrooms and a pet area or dog park (I-5 in California)

kinds.description: Kinds of stops to include; all by default

max_total_fee.description: Most the guest will pay in pet fees for the whole stay, USD

near.description: Start from the route mile nearest this point

paired.description: Also list the paired stops in the window: an exit with people-stops nearby and the nearest dog-legal place (I-5 in California)

response_format.description: 'markdown' for readable text, 'json' for structured data

route.description: Route id. Miles: California follows the Caltrans odometer (I-5 from the Mexican border, US-101 from Los Angeles, Highway 1 from Dana Point, I-15 San Diego to Primm, I-80 San Francisco to the Nevada line, US-50 West Sacramento to Stateline); Nevada routes count mileposts from the California line, matching exit numbers. Routes: I-5 (i-5, 796 miles), US-101 (us-101, 809 miles), Highway 1 (highway-1, 736 miles), I-15 (i-15, 294 miles), I-80 (i-80, 204 miles), US-50 (us-50, 109 miles), I-15 (i-15-nevada, 124 miles), I-80 (i-80-nevada, 410 miles), US-50 (us-50-nevada, 409 miles), US-95 (us-95-nevada, 664 miles), US-93 (us-93-nevada, 526 miles)

name: dogpolicies_route_stops

accepted.description: With bad_input: each argument that could not be read, with the values it accepts

code.description: With an outcome other than ok: not_found, invalid, unavailable

did_you_mean.description: Close matches to what was asked for: towns, places, slugs or brands, best first

nearest.description: When nothing is inside the radius: the nearest places in the data, with distance_miles

next.description: Calls that would answer the question, in words

outcome.description: Absent or ok: a normal answer. no_match: nothing in the data matches, see did_you_mean, nearest and next. bad_input: the arguments cannot be used as given, see next. partial: some of the ids were found, see missing. unavailable: a live source could not be read. None of these is an error.

resolved_from.description: Set when a word was read as the value the tool uses: hotel as lodging, NB as north. Each key is the argument; asked is what was sent, used what it was read as

answer.description: The one-line answer; while a seasonal rule applies today it leads with it (see today)

citation.description: Copy-ready citation: answer, source, date checked, record URL, license

closed_now.description: Present only when Caltrans reports this rest area fully closed now. Live feed data, not a verified rule: check quickmap.dot.ca.gov

fetched_at.description: When the conditions loop read the feed

until.description: Caltrans' end time (ISO); null when no end is set

confidence.description: stated: the place's own source says it; inferred_from_agency: an agency-wide rule; inherited_brand: the chain's policy, not confirmed by this hotel

freshness.description: fresh: inside its review interval; due: past it; stale: past twice it, confirm before you go; unreadable: the last check could not read the source

today.description: Only for a place with seasonal dog rules (plover nesting season, summer beach hours): which applies on the server's date, until when, and which starts next, with the source. Repeat sentence with the answer.

date.description: The date this was computed for: the server's date

rule.description: The seasonal rule in plain words

season.description: When it runs, in the source's dates: "July 1 to May 15"

in_season.description: true: a seasonal rule is in effect on that date; null: the source gives a season without dates

rule.description: The seasonal rule in plain words

season.description: When it runs, in the source's dates: "July 1 to May 15"

sentence.description: Leads answer and citation while a seasonal rule applies or starts within 14 days; null otherwise

rule.description: The seasonal rule in plain words

season.description: When it runs, in the source's dates: "July 1 to May 15"

undated.description: Seasons the source states without dates: not known to apply
